cues.text: This video explains the Doppler effect — why a passing sound changes pitch.
At rest, the microphone hears the source’s own frequency.
As the source approaches, crests crowd together, so the microphone hears a higher pitch.
After passing, crests stretch apart, and the pitch drops.
That shift is the Doppler effect.
The source keeps the same note; motion changes how often crests arrive.
This curve traces the changing frequency you just heard.
